record.original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Does X contain an infinite-dimensional subspace Y such that Y is either reflexive, isomorphic to c₀, or isomorphic to ℓ₁?

artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem in Banach space theory. By a theorem of James, a Banach space with an unconditional basis is reflexive if and only if it contains neither c₀ nor ℓ₁, so the question is closely tied to the existence of unconditional basic sequences. Gowers–Maurey showed that not every infinite-dimensional Banach space contains a subspace with an unconditional basis (hereditarily indecomposable spaces exist), but this does not refute the trichotomy reflexive / c₀ / ℓ₁ at the subspace level. The problem continues to be cited as open in surveys of Banach space theory.

status_evidence.title: Tsirelson space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Tsirelson constructed a reflexive Banach space that does not contain any ℓp or c₀.
status_evidence.claim: Reflexive subspaces without classical structure exist, illustrating that the trichotomy reflexive/c₀/ℓ₁ is the natural weakening of the classical subspace problem.

status_evidence.title: What is a Hereditarily Indecomposable Banach Space?
status_evidence.snippet: Gowers–Maurey constructed Banach spaces with no unconditional basic sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The classical question of unconditional subspaces was settled negatively, but the reflexive/c₀/ℓ₁ subspace question is a related and still discussed problem.
